findings_unaided: Account 4100, Service revenue: S2 says the increase was 28,200 but the table shows this account rose $229,000, a 28.2 percent jump, the dollar figure in the sentence looks like it is missing a digit or got mixed up with the percentage.
Account 4200, Freight billed to customers: down $65,000, a 34.9 percent drop, it is marked over threshold but I do not see a sentence anywhere that explains it.
Account 5100, Inbound freight: S4 says freight declined to $287,800, but the table shows this account rose from $214,000 to $287,800, up $73,800, so the sentence has the direction backwards.
Account 6000, Warehouse wages: up $72,500, an 11.5 percent increase, marked over threshold, but there is no sentence in the commentary that covers it.

Account 6200, Repairs and maintenance, depots: S5 says the roof and dock leveler program finished on June 30, then S9 says the remaining depot repairs are scheduled to finish in August, those two do not agree on whether the work is done.

C1.reason: Fair, $1,600 on software subscriptions is nowhere near the threshold and S8 spends far more words on it than the big unexplained lines get.

C2.reason: Right, the table has account 4100 moving $229,000 and S2 only says 28,200, so the sentence is quoting the wrong scale of number.

C3.reason: That matches what S6 already says, the $19,400 belongs to June and is being pushed into July, so this is a period question worth naming.

C4.reason: Professional fees only moved $7,500, which fails the dollar test in the rule stated at the top, so a full tie-out is not required here.

C5.reason: Agreed, S5 calls the repair program finished on June 30 and S9 says remaining repairs continue into August, those cannot both be accurate.

C6.reason: I did not rework the margin math myself, so I will defer and accept that the rounded 24 percent claim may not hold once unrounded.

C7.reason: S7 states $42,000 for bad debt but the table for account 6400 shows $47,000 moved, so the sentence and the schedule are off from each other.

C8.reason: Agreed, a $72,500 move on warehouse wages that clears the threshold and gets zero mention anywhere is a real gap in the memo.

C9.reason: Checking back, inbound freight rose from $214,000 to $287,800 in the table, so S4 calling that a decline has the direction wrong.

C10.reason: Account 4000 moved $372,000 in the table, not $65,000, so this challenge is pairing the wrong dollar figure with the wrong account.

C11.reason: Depreciation sits at zero movement, $128,000 both months, well under any threshold, and nothing in the memo mentions new depot assets to chase.

C12.reason: Fair, S3 just asserts a Tri-State ramp will keep driving growth through the third quarter and I have not seen anything that backs that up.
